title: Management of Surgical Complications: Ureteric Injury, Fistulae & Bowel Leak: Ureteric Repair, Martius Flap and Anastomotic Dehiscence
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 25
DiSaia and Creasman Clinical Gynecologic Oncology 10th Edition Ch 19
Rock JA, Jones HW. Te Linde's Operative Gynecology 12th Edition

steps.say: The ureter is vulnerable to iatrogenic transection, ligation, or thermal devascularization during radical pelvic gynecological oncology procedures.
steps.tx: The ureter is at hazard at four specific **ureteric injury sites**: crossing the iliac vessels beneath the **infundibulopelvic ligament**, within the ovarian fossa, during lateral **uterine artery crossing** in the cardinal tunnel, and at the **bladder trigone insertion** during radical bladder mobilization.

vis.caption: Relation of the uterine artery to the ureter near the cervix and pelvic lymph nodes. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Anatomical drawing showing the ureter passing under the uterine artery water under the bridge near the supravaginal cervix.

steps.say: When a ureteric injury occurs in the distal pelvic ureter close to the urinary bladder, ureteral reimplantation represents the treatment of choice.
steps.tx: For distal pelvic injuries (**distal third injury <4-5 cm** from the bladder), **ureteroneocystostomy** with anti-reflux submucosal tunnel is performed over a **double-J stent**, combined with a **psoas hitch** or **Boari flap** to eliminate all anastomotic tension. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

rows: Psoas bladder hitch or Boari tubularized flap
Middle Third (pelvic brim to ischial spine)
Nephrostomy drainage followed by delayed reconstruction

steps.say: Primary end-to-end ureteral anastomosis is appropriate for mid-ureteric transections when adequate length permits a completely tension-free closure.
steps.tx: For clean **mid-ureteric transection**, end-to-end **ureteroureterostomy** is performed over a double-J stent using **spatulated tension-free** margins and interrupted **4-0/5-0 absorbable** monofilament sutures, preserving adventitial blood supply to prevent ischemic stricture formation. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Identify mid-ureteric transection and debride devascularized margins
Spatulate both ureteric ends 5 mm obliquely on opposite surfaces
Pass double-J ureteral stent across anastomosis into renal pelvis and bladder
Close with interrupted 4-0 or 5-0 PDS sutures in a watertight tension-free fashion

steps.say: Vesicovaginal fistula following radical pelvic surgery or radiation therapy presents with pathognomonic symptoms and requires objective dye testing.
steps.tx: A **vesicovaginal fistula (VVF)** typically presents 7 to 14 days postoperatively with **continuous watery leakage** despite normal voiding. Clinical diagnosis is verified using the classic **double-dye test** with oral **methylene blue and phenazopyridine** to distinguish vesical from ureteric leakage. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Double-Dye Test Interpretation
points: Oral phenazopyridine turns urine orange; intravesical methylene blue turns urine blue
Blue staining on vaginal swab confirms vesicovaginal fistula (bladder origin)
Orange staining on vaginal swab confirms ureterovaginal fistula (ureteric origin)

right.title: Clinical Presentation Features
points: Continuous, involuntary, painless watery vaginal fluid leakage
Patient may continue to void normal volumes intermittently
Onset typically delayed 7 to 14 days due to ischemic tissue necrosis

steps.say: Surgical repair of complex or post-radiation vesicovaginal fistulae requires complete excision of scarred tissue and interposition of healthy vascularized flaps.
steps.tx: Complex or **radiation fistula repair** mandates tension-free multilayer closure and interposition of a vascularized **Martius flap** (fibrofatty **bulbocavernosus fat pad**) or **omental interposition**, accompanied by continuous transurethral bladder decompression with **catheterization 14-21 days** postoperatively. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Excise dense fibrotic fistula tract completely back to soft pliable tissue edges
Mobilize bladder mucosa and muscularis separately from anterior vaginal wall
Harvest labial Martius bulbocavernosus fat pad flap on posterior vascular pedicle
Tunnel flap into vagina, interpose between suture lines, and maintain catheter for 14-21 days

steps.say: Gastrointestinal anastomotic dehiscence following bowel resection during cytoreduction is a life-threatening complication that requires early recognition.
steps.tx: Gastrointestinal **anastomotic leak** or unrecognized thermal perforation characteristically manifests between **postoperative days 4-7** with unexplained **tachycardia and acidosis**, oliguria, abdominal distension, **elevated CRP**, and feculent peritoneal drain output. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

rows: CRP fail to normalize or rises > 150 mg/L
Frank feculent, purulent, or enteric contents

steps.say: Suspected anastomotic breakdown with peritonitis or clinical sepsis mandates immediate operative re-exploration and fecal diversion.
steps.tx: Septic anastomotic breakdown mandates urgent **exploratory laparotomy**, aggressive debridement, copious **peritoneal lavage**, and **exteriorization as stoma** (such as a **Hartmann procedure** for rectosigmoid disruption), strictly avoiding attempted primary re-anastomosis in a heavily contaminated peritoneal bed. Rapid source control and delayed reconstruction minimize overall septic mortality.

left.title: Mandatory Emergency Interventions
points: Immediate aggressive fluid resuscitation and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
Exteriorization of compromised bowel segments with stoma creation

right.title: Prohibited Surgical Practices
points: Never attempt simple oversewing or primary re-anastomosis in sepsis
Never rely on conservative percutaneous drainage if peritonitis is present
Do not delay laparotomy for serial imaging in decompensating patients

steps.say: Rectovaginal fistulae following low anterior resection or pelvic exenteration require immediate diversion with delayed definitive anatomical reconstruction.
steps.tx: Development of a **rectovaginal fistula** requires immediate **proximal fecal diversion** via **loop colostomy** or loop ileostomy. Definitive tissue repair is deliberately postponed for a **delayed repair 3-6 months** to allow acute inflammation, pelvic edema, and radiation reaction to completely subside.
